name: Ingress: host + path routing
objective: CKA › Services & Networking. An Ingress is L7 HTTP routing rules (host + path → Service:port) realized by an ingress controller via an IngressClass. Create a host rule to one Service, then add path-based routing to a second. Graded on the Ingress spec (this bench has no ingress controller; the object is what the exam checks).

questions.title: Route a host to a Service
questions.teach:
An **Ingress** maps HTTP `host` + `path` to a backend `Service:port`. `spec.ingressClassName` picks which controller implements it. A `pathType` of `Prefix` matches by path prefix; `Exact` matches the whole path.

**Gotcha:** Ingress routes to a **Service**, not pods directly — the Service must exist and have endpoints. `kubectl create ingress` is the fast path: `--rule='host/path=svc:port'`.
questions.prompt:
The Services `web` and `api` (both port 80) already exist in `ingress-learn`. Create an Ingress `shop` (ingressClassName `nginx`) that routes host `shop.example.com` path `/` (pathType `Prefix`) to Service `web:80`.

Target: Ingress `shop` has ingressClassName `nginx` and a rule host=shop.example.com, path `/` Prefix → web:80.
questions.hint: `kubectl -n ingress-learn create ingress shop --class=nginx --rule='shop.example.com/*=web:80'` (the `/*` gives pathType Prefix). Or write the YAML with `pathType: Prefix` and `backend.service.name: web`.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata: { name: shop, namespace: ingress-learn }
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
  - host: shop.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend:
          service:
            name: web
            port:
              number: 80
YAML

verification.description: Ingress shop: class nginx, host shop.example.com path / Prefix -> web:80

questions.title: Add path-based routing
questions.teach:
A single host can fan out by path: add another path entry under the same host routing to a different Service. The controller matches the most specific path first.

**Gotcha:** `Prefix` `/api` matches `/api` and `/api/...`; ordering in the manifest doesn't decide precedence — longest-matching path wins at request time.
questions.prompt:
Extend Ingress `shop`: under host `shop.example.com`, add path `/api` (pathType `Prefix`) routing to Service `api:80` (keep the `/` → web:80 rule).

Target: Ingress `shop` has both paths under shop.example.com — `/` → web:80 and `/api` → api:80.
questions.hint: Edit the Ingress and add a second `paths` entry: `path: /api, pathType: Prefix, backend.service.name: api, port 80`. `kubectl -n ingress-learn edit ingress shop` or re-apply the full YAML with both paths.
questions.solution:
cat <<'YAML' | kubectl apply -f -
apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: Ingress
metadata: { name: shop, namespace: ingress-learn }
spec:
  ingressClassName: nginx
  rules:
  - host: shop.example.com
    http:
      paths:
      - path: /
        pathType: Prefix
        backend: { service: { name: web, port: { number: 80 } } }
      - path: /api
        pathType: Prefix
        backend: { service: { name: api, port: { number: 80 } } }
YAML

verification.description: Ingress shop has /api Prefix -> api:80 alongside / -> web:80
